title: Horizon Quantum Signs Letter of Intent to Acquire Entropica Labs for $27 Million - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Horizon Quantum (Nasdaq: HQ) signed a non-binding LOI to acquire Singapore QEC software firm Entropica Labs for $27M in Class A shares. The deal would merge Entropica's Loom QEC compiler with Horizon's Triple Alpha IDE to compile high-level code directly into fault-tolerant circuits.

insights.claim: Horizon Quantum Holdings signed a non-binding letter of intent to acquire Singapore-based fault-tolerance software company Entropica Labs in an all-equity deal with anticipated consideration of $27 million in Horizon Quantum Class A ordinary shares.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: An all-stock deal shows newly listed quantum companies using their public equity as acquisition currency to consolidate the software layer.
insights.quote: an all-equity transaction valued at an anticipated consideration of $27 million
insights.locator: Quantum software developer Horizon Quantum Holdings

insights.claim: The Horizon Quantum acquisition of Entropica Labs remains subject to due diligence, financial audits, definitive agreements and regulatory approvals, so it may not close on the stated terms.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Non-binding status means execution risk; investors should not treat the deal as certain.
insights.locator: Quantum software developer Horizon Quantum Holdings

insights.claim: Entropica Labs develops Loom, a QEC compiler that lets hardware manufacturers add error-corrected logical operations to their QPUs without building full QEC toolchains themselves.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Outsourced QEC tooling for hardware makers is a possible picks-and-shovels business as the industry moves to logical qubits.
insights.locator: The combination unites two prominent startups

insights.claim: Horizon Quantum's Triple Alpha development environment lets classical software developers compile hardware-agnostic quantum algorithms without manual circuit gate mapping.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hardware-agnostic tooling positions Horizon as an abstraction layer, valuable if the hardware market stays fragmented.
insights.locator: The combination unites two prominent startups

insights.claim: Combining Loom with Triple Alpha aims to automate end-to-end translation of high-level code into fault-tolerant circuits, treating application synthesis and error correction as one integrated stack rather than separate layers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: If logical processors mature, software vendors that own the full compile path to fault-tolerant circuits could capture more value than those at a single layer.
insights.quote: Rather than treating application synthesis and error correction as disjoint layers
insights.locator: Integrating Entropica’s QEC architecture into Horizon’s

insights.claim: The deal targets the emerging industry shift from physical gate compilation to logical fault-tolerant computing and would extend Horizon's reach across hardware builders and enterprise software developers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Signals that QEC software is becoming a strategic asset worth acquiring ahead of commercial logical processors.
insights.quote: the emerging transition from physical gate compilation to logical fault-tolerant computing
insights.locator: Integrating Entropica’s QEC architecture into Horizon’s

insights.claim: Horizon Quantum (founded 2018 by Joe Fitzsimons) and Entropica Labs (founded 2018 by former Centre for Quantum Technologies researchers Tommaso Demarie and Ewan Munro) are both products of Singapore's quantum ecosystem.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Points to Singapore's CQT-centered ecosystem as a source of quantum software startups and consolidation.
insights.locator: The combination unites two prominent startups
